sense: pleased with what one has or has done

terms.gloss: be proud of, pride oneself on; boast
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent: with the ablative, with dē or in and the ablative, or with an accusative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.16.8: nōn enim mihi videor īnsolenter glōriārī
Traupman 156: glōrior (+ abl., dē or in), to be proud of
terms.comment: Pride that speaks: to glory in something, and so often to boast (Lewis & Short). For a parent’s quiet pride in a child, Latin says the joy instead: gaudeō, laetor (see glad).

terms.grammar: adjective: with the ablative of the cause
terms.register: in hōc sēnsū vōx poētica et post Augustum: Verg., Mart., Sen.
evidence: Mart. 10.37.17–19: vēnātor captā maele superbus adest
terms.comment: In classical prose superbus is haughty, arrogant (see proud, arrogant); the good sense, proud of something, splendid, is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.1.4: glōriae quidem videō fore
Traupman 156: glōria, pride, source of pride
terms.comment: “It is something to be proud of”: glōriae est, with the double dative.

phrases.latin: idem ego ille (nōn enim mihi videor īnsolenter glōriārī cum dē mē apud tē loquor, in eā praesertim epistulā quam nōlō aliīs legī) idem inquam ego recreāvī adflīctōs animōs bonōrum
phrases.english: it was I, the same man (for I don’t think I’m being immodestly proud when I speak of myself to you, especially in a letter I don’t want others to read), I say, who revived the spirits of the loyal men
What, are you proud that it turned out as you wanted?

phrases.latin: dum loquor, ecce redit sportā piscātor inānī, vēnātor captā maele superbus adest: omnis ab urbānō venit ad mare cēna macellō
phrases.english: as I speak, look, the fisherman comes back with an empty basket, the hunter arrives proud of the badger he caught: the whole dinner by the sea comes from the town market

sources: Lewis & Short: glorior · Lewis & Short: superbus · Lewis & Short: gloria
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 156.
